rules.statement: When a file is generated from a template or shared partial, make the fix in the source template and regenerate every copy, rather than editing one generated copy by hand.
rules.why: The build regenerates the copies from the template, so an edit to a copy is overwritten and the other copies keep the bad wording.
rules.check: Look for a diff that changes generated prompt, skill, agent or command files without the matching change to their source template, or that changes the template without regenerating its copies.

rules.statement: Text in a shared partial must be true for every file that includes it: make a step that only some includers perform conditional ("When you write X, …"), or move it into the template that needs it.
rules.why: A shared sentence telling every includer to do something only one of them does leads a model to look for a file that doesn't exist or make a stray commit. Wording that fits only commands confuses users of agents that include the same partial.
rules.check: When a partial or included section changes, check each file that includes it and confirm that every instruction and phrase ("run this command", "commit the record") applies to that file.

rules.statement: In agent or prompt instructions, state a condition in terms of a concrete value the tool or script prints (for example "when the state script's `renumber` line names a version"), not as a vague description that can be read either way round.
rules.why: Wording like "when the entry before it landed with the version it expected" can be read as inverted, so a model might skip a needed step or add one that isn't needed.
rules.check: Look for conditional instructions in prompts or skills that describe a state in prose when a script output line exists that decides it, and for wording whose trigger could be read backwards.

rules.statement: When a script adds a fallback value or an exclusion branch (a placeholder title, skipping an entry that doesn't match, keeping an entry out of a second list), add a test that asserts the output for that branch.
rules.why: An untested fallback or exclusion can regress without anyone noticing, for example a worktree listed twice or a missing placeholder.
rules.check: For new branches that substitute a placeholder, skip an item, or decide which of two lists an item goes in, look for a test case that covers each branch and asserts the resulting output lines.

rules.statement: Don't report a `Test-Path` (or other existence check) on a worktree path reported by `git worktree list` as redundant: git still lists prunable worktrees whose folders were deleted.
rules.why: The maintainer kept the guard because `git worktree list` can report a prunable worktree whose directory no longer exists.
rules.check: Before flagging an existence check as redundant, see whether the path comes from `git worktree list` or a similar listing that can include stale entries.
